subject: Brightline — reference deployment & solution gate review
messages:
From: Amelia Cross <amelia@brightline.io>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@brightline.io
Date: Thu, 8 Jan 2026 18:22:00 -0500
Subject: Brightline — Redwood reference deployment & validation kickoff

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this on. We're excited to move forward with Redwood as our preferred inference runtime for customer deployments. Attached is a short integration proposal and a network drawing that show our planned connector and where we expect to co-locate inference calls. Before we lock schedules, can your team confirm the following so we can align internal engineering resources: 

1) Supported TLS ciphers and mutual-TLS expectations for Private deployments (we currently support mTLS with client certs).
2) Max concurrent sessions per connector host we should design for (baseline traffic: ~120 req/s, peak 450 req/s).
3) Guidance on prefix/KV caching behavior and recommended cache TTLs for conversational workloads.
4) Any kernel/quantization profiles you recommend for a 7B dense T5 variant to keep token latency under 50ms on g5-like hardware.

Proposed week: Jan 12-16 for a 60m technical review call. We can prep a short demo showing a local connector running against a sandbox.

Attachments: brightline-integration-proposal.pdf, network-drawing.vsdx

Happy to adapt — let me know what you need from our side.

Best,
Amelia Cross
Director of Platform Engineering
Brightline Systems

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Amelia Cross <amelia@brightline.io>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightline — Redwood reference deployment & validation kickoff

Amelia — thanks, received the proposal and the network diagram. We'll run the technical review and validation against our Private reference stack. Proposed agenda for the 60m call: 

- 5m intro + success criteria
- 10m Brightline architecture walkthrough (you)
- 15m Redwood runtime expectations + network requirements (us)
- 20m compatibility / integration gaps and required artifacts
- 10m next steps and schedule for validation milestones

To prepare we need the following artifacts from Brightline before the meeting (ideally 48h prior):
- connector manifest (Dockerfile + manifest.yaml or OCI image ref)
- expected request/response schemas (example payloads)
- cert provisioning flow for mTLS (how you rotate certs)
- perf profile for your connector (local qps, concurrency model)

Internal owners: Sergio will lead runtime compatibility and smoke testing, Jonas will handle networking & egress/VPC patterns, Kimberly will coordinate SOW/license and procurement items.

Can you do Jan 14, 10:00–11:00 PT? If not, we have spots on 12 and 15.

Thanks — will attach our validation checklist after we've aligned internally.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Brightline validation — owners & quick checklist

Team — quick internal note ahead of the call. I've sketched a lightweight validation checklist we can use to gate the partner integration (I will put a formal spreadsheet in the shared Drive):

Runtime compatibility (Sergio)
- Pull partner image and run in sandbox with our runtime shim (task: smoke request path)
- Verify tokenization/encoding parity for their payloads (example curl to validate)
  - Example: curl -X POST https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d @sample.json
- Check KV cache behavior with 1k sample convs (observe hit rate and latency)

Networking & Security (Jonas)
- Validate mTLS handshake and cert chain against our CA (we prefer automated rotation + CRL/OCSP checks)
- Confirm egress rules and idle-timeout recommendations for long-lived connections

Commercial & Ops (Kimberly)
- Confirm license model for distributed connector (per-host or per-tenant), any constraints for Dedicated vs Private
- Confirm logging/audit hooks required for SOC2 evidence

Logistics / schedule
- Jan 14: tech review call (confirm with Amelia)
- Jan 18: partner hands over connector image + manifests to our sandbox
- Jan 20–22: internal smoke and perf runs (Sergio leads)

I'll prepare the redwood-validation-template.xlsx and share a Drive link. If we find a high risk item on the call, we'll escalate to Neha for prioritization with GTM/Legal.

— Sergio
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Amelia Cross <amelia@brightline.io>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: eng@brightline.io
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 08:44:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Brightline — Redwood reference deployment & validation kickoff

Neha / team — thanks for the agenda and checklist. Jan 14 at 10:00 PT works for us. Attaching the connector manifest and a short architecture yaml plus a PNG of the customer data flows. Answers to your numbered questions below: 

> 1) TLS / mTLS
We use mutual TLS with client certs. Supported ciphers are ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256. Cert rotation is automated via an internal CA; we can export the rotation process and an example cert bundle.

> 2) Concurrent sessions
Baseline concurrency per host: 150 active requests, burst to 600 if autoscaled. Connector threads are async; connection pooling is used.

> 3) Caching
We rely on short-lived KV caching. Recommended TTL for conversational contexts is 30–120s depending on turn density; we can expose a TTL param in the connector config.

> 4) Quantization / kernel guidance
We do not force model knobs client-side; we'd welcome Redwood's recommendation for a 7B T5-like dense model. Separately, we plan to ship an fp16 build for faster inference but can toggle to int8 if you recommend.

Attachments: brightline-connector-arch.yaml, customer-data-flows.png

Quoted for context:
On Fri, Jan 9, 2026 at 09:03 AM Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Amelia — thanks, received the proposal and the network diagram. We'll run the technical review and validation against our Private reference stack. Proposed agenda for the 60m call: ...

We'll upload the images + manifests to the shared Drive (see Slack channel #partners-brightline) and post the link after the call.

See you Thu.

— Amelia
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Brightline follow-up & next steps (post-call)

Team — quick summary from today's call and actions: 

Call outcome (Jan 14)
- Alignment on mTLS ciphers and cert automation (Brightline will provide rotation docs).
- No hard blockers identified for Private; main work is perf tuning for target latency at peak load.
- Brightline will hand off connector image + manifest to our sandbox on Jan 18 (as agreed).

Open risks / mitigation
- Perf risk: their peak concurrent design (600 burst) is aggressive. Sergio to run perf profile and map autoscaling thresholds (initial estimate: need to validate with 3x traffic spike).
- Config risk: caching TTLs will need harmonization; Jonas to validate KV cache behavior with their TTL param.

Owners & next steps
- Sergio: run smoke + perf runs (Jan 20–22). Deliverable: perf report + suggested model quantization profile.
- Jonas: verify mTLS handshake + egress rules in sandbox (Jan 18–19). Deliverable: network acceptance note.
- Kimberly: finalize SOW template and licensing question (confirm if per-host or per-tenant) by Jan 21.
- Neha: consolidate findings and prepare partner-readiness brief for Alliances by Jan 25.

Artifacts received (Drive): brightline-integration-proposal.pdf, network-drawing.vsdx, brightline-connector-arch.yaml, customer-data-flows.png
Template uploaded: redwood-validation-template.xlsx (I'll add checklist entries for perf & security).

If anyone spots a missing item, flag in the thread. If perf shows repeated regressions, we'll consider a short canary with limited customers.

Thanks — I'll ping Amelia to confirm Jan 18 handoff once Jonas signs off on the cert handshake.

Neha Kapoor
Partner Solutions, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
